root_cause: Connector changes need one cross-domain review even if technical test/plan/sovereignty controls authorize execution. Browser clients could previously set state=Active, forge review fields, or reuse stale evidence.
prevention: Re-use the existing tenant connector review queue for pending cross-domain events, with safe human-readable domain and ESRS candidates.

Keep open ESRS/CSRD applicability and materiality reviews in the existing tenant queue after separately authorized connector activation; do not convert technical success into a compliance claim or create a permanent activation deadlock.
Server forces drafts to Draft state and ignores browser-supplied authorization/review objects.
Increment connector configuration version on real changes to invalidate stale test proof; distinguish operational readbacks from configuration changes.

evidence.outcome: Server-side Draft enforcement, config version invalidation, tenant-scoped pending review queue and separate independently verified technical activation with impactReviewPending. Customer-authorized review closure still needs authoritative evidence.
